explanation: Winston Churchill made the phrase famous in a 1946 speech in Fulton, Missouri, describing a line from Stettin (modern Szczecin) on the Baltic to Trieste on the Adriatic.

claims.text: The 'Iron Curtain' was the Cold War boundary dividing Europe between the Soviet-dominated communist east and the west.
The term 'Iron Curtain' referred to Europe, not to Asia, Africa or South America.
Winston Churchill popularized the phrase 'iron curtain' in a speech at Fulton, Missouri, in March 1946.
Churchill described the curtain as running from Stettin in the Baltic to Trieste in the Adriatic.
Stettin is the city known in Polish as Szczecin.
